fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Queuing/turning/parking interference at closely-spaced intersections on a corridor with recorded high-accident designations is a substantive preliminary-design safety issue.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is backed by a verbatim quote (EV-US-016) matching the recorded case-study issue and location; no invented content detected.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed strictly as a safety_concern with null normative basis note; no compliance question is conflated with the safety issue.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific and actionable—turning-movement restrictions plus relocation of identified stalls clear of the intersection functional area—and viable at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged along the commercial corridor but scoped out because the conflict mechanism is vehicle-to-vehicle; not applicable yet acknowledged.

justifications.substance: Queue spillback between signalized intersections ~650 ft apart on a corridor with recorded high-accident designations is a substantive, well-recognized preliminary-design safety mechanism, not a vacuous observation.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal 650-ft spacing claim rests on a verbatim quoted evidence item (EV-US-001) corroborated as recorded scheme data (TABLE A.1), and the spillback inference is transparently labeled as derived, with no invented content.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Properly framed as a safety_concern with null normative basis, keeping the operational/safety question categorically distinct from any compliance determination under FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommends concrete, viable countermeasures—signal coordination, Do Not Block Intersection signs, and enhanced conspicuity of signing/displays—all actionable at the preliminary design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are acknowledged as crossing both signalized intersections, but their exposure (e.g., crosswalk blockage or signal violation induced by spilled-back queues) is not analyzed; impacts are treated as not applicable to the stated mechanism and merely acknowledged.
